summary:
A mobile-first, climate-smart farming adviser for smallholder farmers in the Philippines. We piloted it in Valencia City, Bukidnon.

Farmers pick a crop (rice, corn, or tobacco), mark their field on a map, and choose a planting window. Our STRATA crop model then checks that choice against decades of local climate data and returns three things: how likely planting is to succeed, a climate-compatibility score, and the best date to plant. Each result comes with a plain-language reason, such as expected dry spells, heavy-rain days, or extreme heat.

Live Open-Meteo forecasts and readings from a soil sensor in the field turn this into daily advice, for example, holding off on fertilizer before heavy rain. "Tata," an AI adviser, answers "what if" questions in Filipino, Cebuano, or English, with read-aloud and voice input. A community feed connects farmers with each other and with official DA and NIA advisories.

This matters because changing rainfall and rising heat are making traditional planting calendars unreliable, and one badly timed season can wipe out a smallholder's income. Strata puts climate science into farmers' own language, which they already carry on the phone.
details:
Strata: a planting adviser in a farmer's pocket

What it does: Strata helps rice, corn and tobacco farmers in Valencia City, Bukidnon pick the best day to plant. The farmer chooses a crop, pins the field on a map and sets a planting window. Our STRATA model checks that window against 10 years of NASA POWER weather and FAO EcoCrop crop needs. It returns a likelihood rating, a climate score and the best date, each with plain-language reasons. The app also has:

  • a 16-day weather forecast
  • a field sensor that tracks water level, soil moisture and temperature, and alerts the farmer when to irrigate
  • a fertilizer warning before heavy rain
  • a season outlook
  • Tata, an AI farming assistant
  • a community feed for farmers and advisers

Benefits: Fewer failed crops, and less wasted water and fertilizer. Every recommendation explains why. It works in English, Filipino and Bisaya and can read answers aloud. It keeps working when the internet or the sensor drops.

Intended impact: Help smallholder farmers cope with dry spells, heavy rain and heat by putting NASA data behind their planting decisions. That should mean better yields and less pollution in irrigation canals.

Tools: JavaScript, React, Vite, Tailwind CSS, Leaflet, Chart.js; Python, FastAPI, SQLite; Google Gemini; NASA POWER, Open-Meteo and FAO EcoCrop data; an in-field IoT sensor; the browser's speech features.

Creativity: It combines 10 years of climate history, the live forecast and real-time field readings into one answer. "Tata" is named after a familiar elder figure, not presented as a faceless chatbot. Simple rules turn expert farming advice into everyday decisions.

Factors considered: Farmers' literacy levels, the languages they speak and the phones they already own. Fit to the local crops and barangays. Weak rural internet. Keeping costs low with free data sources. Keeping API keys secure. A scientific basis for the model. Environmental impact.
